title: Wisconsin's 8th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Wisconsin's 8th Congressional District pits first-term Republican incumbent Tony Wied against a trio of Democratic primary contenders in a northeast Wisconsin district that includes Green Bay, Appleton, and Door County. The district has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of R+8 and has been held by Republicans since 1999. The Democratic primary — the party's first competitive primary in this district in nearly 20 years — features retired Army Lt. Colonel and former Green Bay School Board member Rick Crosson, retired businessman and former teacher Mark Scheffler, and musician Katrina deVille. The primary is set for August 11, 2026, and the general election is November 3, 2026.
polling_note: No specific public opinion polls were found for Wisconsin's 8th Congressional District race in 2026. Cook Political Report rates the district as 'Solid R.'

candidates.name: Tony Wied
candidates.summary: Tony Wied is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 8th Congressional District, first elected in 2024. A businessman and political outsider, Wied owned and operated Dino Stop gas stations and Little Caesars restaurants in Northeast Wisconsin before selling his businesses in 2022. He is endorsed by President Donald Trump and focuses his campaign on border security, curbing government spending, American energy independence, and supporting Trump's America First agenda.

candidates.name: Rick Crosson
candidates.summary: Rick Crosson is a retired U.S. Army Lieutenant Colonel and Master Army Aviator running as a Democrat for Wisconsin's 8th Congressional District. He served 20 years in the Army, flying surveillance missions along the Iron Curtain and later serving as U.S. Military Liaison to Mexico. After retiring from the military, he worked in the logistics and transportation industry in Green Bay and served on the Green Bay Area Board of Education. His campaign emphasizes affordability, accountability in government, and healthcare as a right.

candidates.name: Mark Scheffler
candidates.summary: Mark Scheffler is a retired businessman and former public school teacher running as a progressive Democrat for Wisconsin's 8th Congressional District. A lifelong Wisconsin resident and son of a dairy farmer, Scheffler founded and led a successful business that generated over $100 million in economic growth in Northeast Wisconsin. He emphasizes running an independent-minded campaign funded by small-dollar donors through his '50x4 People's Pledge,' and focuses on sustainable economic, social, and environmental policies.

candidates.name: Katrina deVille
candidates.summary: Katrina deVille is a musician, bandleader, and small business owner running as a Democratic Socialist for Wisconsin's 8th Congressional District. A transgender woman and lifelong Wisconsin resident, she attended the University of Wisconsin-Green Bay for Jazz Studies and has performed in 30 states and 7 countries with her band. She also owns a custom auto shop. If elected, she would become the second openly transgender person to serve in Congress. Her campaign advocates for Medicare for All, a $22 minimum wage, taxing the rich, and body autonomy.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific public opinion polls exist for this race, which reduces confidence. However, the structural fundamentals are strongly Republican: the district has a Cook PVI of R+8, Republicans have held the seat continuously since 1999, and the incumbent Tony Wied (first elected 2024) is running for re-election. The Democratic side features a contested three-way primary (Crosson, Scheffler, deVille) with no clearly dominant general-election challenger yet established, and the primary isn't until August 11, 2026. Cook Political Report rates the district 'Solid R.' Taken together, the evidence supports Republicans as overwhelming favorites despite the absence of polling.
